description:
The Kashyapa Scheme for Food & Shelter was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This scheme aims to provide food and shelter to the homeless and those living in extreme poverty. 

The initiative is named after the ancient sage Kashyapa, symbolizing nourishment and care. 

The primary objective of the Kashyapa Scheme is to ensure that no individual goes hungry or lacks shelter. 

The scheme targets the most vulnerable sections of society, including street dwellers and those without permanent housing. 

The government has set a measurable target of providing food and shelter to at least 1 million individuals in its first year. 

The scheme aims to reduce the number of homeless individuals in urban areas by 30 percent by 2025. 

Under this scheme, beneficiaries receive a daily meal and access to temporary shelters. 

The daily meal includes a nutritious package valued at INR 50. 

Each beneficiary is entitled to three meals a day, amounting to INR 150 daily. 

The temporary shelters are equipped with basic amenities such as bedding, sanitation facilities, and clean drinking water. 

The government allocates a budget of INR 500 crores annually for the Kashyapa Scheme. 

This budget is intended to cover food supplies, shelter maintenance, and administrative costs. 

Eligibility for the Kashyapa Scheme is determined by specific criteria. 

Individuals must be at least 18 years old to qualify for assistance. 

There are no income limits for eligibility, as the scheme targets the most marginalized populations. 

However, preference is given to individuals from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes. 

Applications can be submitted online through the official government portal. 

The application process requires individuals to provide proof of identity, such as an Aadhaar card or voter ID. 

Additionally, applicants must submit a self-declaration stating their current living conditions. 

The application form can be accessed on the MyScheme portal at www.myscheme.gov.in. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by local authorities within 15 days. 

Approved beneficiaries are then notified via SMS or email. 

Disbursement of benefits occurs on a monthly basis. 

Each beneficiary receives a food card that allows them to access meals at designated centers. 

These centers are located in urban areas where the homeless population is concentrated. 

The shelters are managed by local non-governmental organizations in collaboration with the government. 

The government conducts regular audits to ensure compliance with the scheme's standards. 

The shelters are open 24 hours a day to accommodate individuals at any time. 

In addition to food and shelter, the scheme also provides access to healthcare services. 

Beneficiaries can receive basic medical care through tie-ups with local health clinics. 

The government aims to provide health check-ups for all beneficiaries at least once every three months. 

The Kashyapa Scheme also includes provisions for skill development programs. 

These programs are designed to help beneficiaries gain employment and improve their livelihoods. 

Workshops on vocational skills are conducted regularly at the shelters. 

The government collaborates with various skill development agencies to implement these programs. 

Feedback mechanisms are in place to assess the effectiveness of the scheme. 

Beneficiaries are encouraged to provide input on the services they receive. 

The government uses this feedback to make necessary adjustments to the program. 

The Kashyapa Scheme is part of a broader initiative to combat poverty and homelessness in India. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The scheme is monitored by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. 

Local municipal bodies are responsible for the implementation of the scheme at the ground level. 

The government has partnered with various NGOs to enhance the reach of the scheme. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform potential beneficiaries about the scheme. 

These campaigns utilize social media, local newspapers, and community meetings. 

The government has reported that over 500,000 individuals have benefited from the scheme since its launch. 

The success of the Kashyapa Scheme is measured through regular surveys and assessments. 

The government aims to expand the scheme to cover more rural areas in the future. 

Plans are in place to increase the budget allocation to INR 1,000 crores by 2025. 

This increase will allow for the establishment of more shelters and food distribution centers. 

The Kashyapa Scheme represents a significant step towards ensuring food security and shelter for all. 

It reflects the government's commitment to social welfare and poverty alleviation. 

The scheme is expected to evolve based on the changing needs of the population. 

Continuous monitoring and evaluation will help in refining the objectives and benefits. 

As of October 2023, the Kashyapa Scheme remains a crucial initiative in India's welfare landscape. 

It highlights the importance of addressing homelessness and food insecurity in urban settings. 

The scheme serves as a model for similar initiatives in other countries facing similar challenges. 

Overall, the Kashyapa Scheme for Food & Shelter is a comprehensive approach to tackling poverty. 

It provides immediate relief while also focusing on long-term solutions for the homeless population. 

The government's proactive stance in implementing this scheme is commendable. 

It underscores the need for collaborative efforts between various stakeholders. 

The involvement of local communities and organizations is vital for the scheme's success. 

The Kashyapa Scheme is a testament to India's ongoing efforts to uplift its most vulnerable citizens. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a more inclusive society. 

The scheme's focus on nutrition, shelter, and skill development is a holistic approach to welfare. 

As the program continues to develop, it is expected to make a lasting impact on the lives of many.
